_meta.name: OFFICE iQ — Project Pack DUMMY TEMPLATE (rules-only, no real content)
_meta.purpose: Hand this file to another repo/team so they can generate ONE JSON file describing their own project — company + tickets + DSA problems + quiz — in the exact shape OFFICE iQ's importer expects. Every field below is either a placeholder (replace the <ANGLE_BRACKET> value) or a working minimal example showing the shape. This whole `_meta` block is ignored on import (unknown top-level keys are stripped) — it exists purely to document the rules inline.
howToUse: 1. Fill in `company` — this becomes the catalog/workspace entry.
2. Replace the sample `tickets` entries with real ones — one ticket per simulation day, day 1..30, no duplicate days, at most 30 total.
3. Replace the sample `dsaProblems` — at most 30, paired to tickets either by matching `day` or, if `day` is omitted, by position (1st DSA -> 1st ticket, 2nd -> 2nd, ...).
4. Replace the sample `quizQuestions` — at most 200, each MUST have exactly 4 `options` and a `correctIndex` in 0..3.
5. Delete this `_meta` block (optional — it's stripped automatically) and upload the file via the admin Catalog screen's 'Import project (.json)' button.
6. On success this ONE upload creates the catalog entry AND its tickets/DSA/quiz in one shot. Re-uploading the same `slug` later is a 409 (no upsert) — pick a slug you're sure is new.
_meta.validationOrder: The whole file is normalized BEFORE anything is written to the database (normalizeContentPack runs against your `company` block first). An invalid file returns 422 with a `details` array listing every problem found — no partial/orphan data is ever created.

hardLimits.tickets: 1 to 30 items, one per simulation day (1..30), each day used at most once
hardLimits.dsaProblems: 0 to 30 items (optional, but pairing with tickets is how DSA problems reach candidates)
hardLimits.quizQuestions: 0 to 200 items (optional; each question needs exactly 4 options)

notes: `company.slug` must be lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens only, and must not already exist in the catalog.

`tickets[].day` is optional per item — if omitted, the item's position in the array (1st = day 1, 2nd = day 2, ...) is used instead. Prefer setting it explicitly so re-ordering the array can't silently change days.
`tickets[].ticketId` is optional — if omitted one is generated from the domain + day.
`dsaProblems[].day` links a problem to a ticket's day; if omitted, DSA problems pair to tickets positionally.
`quizQuestions[].correctIndex` and `.explanation` are stored server-side and never sent to candidates before they submit — write real answers, they are not shown early.
Malformed quiz questions are silently dropped (not fatal); malformed tickets/DSA make the whole upload fail with a 422 and a details list, so fix everything the response flags.
Only 2 sample `tickets`/1 sample `dsaProblems`/1 sample `quizQuestions` are shown below to keep this template short — copy those objects to add more, up to the hard limits above (30/30/200).

company.name: <COMPANY_OR_PROJECT_DISPLAY_NAME>
company.category: <BACKEND | FULLSTACK | FRONTEND | MOBILE | AI | DEVOPS | DATA>
company.description: <longer description of the simulated codebase/product, max 4000 chars>
company.objective: <what a candidate should demonstrate by the end of 30 days, max 2000 chars>
company.domainDetails: <domain-specific context a candidate needs, max 2000 chars>

tickets.title: <short ticket title, max 200 chars>
tickets.description: <full ticket description a candidate reads before starting, max 4000 chars>

tickets.title: <example: a real feature/bug/security ticket>
tickets.description: <describe the concrete task, the file(s)/area involved, and how it's verified>

quizQuestions.question: <MCQ question text, max 500 chars>
quizQuestions.explanation: <why the correct option is right, shown to candidates only after they submit>
